features.quote: Measure, don't manufacture. The harness must elicit and score the behavior, never train, fine-tune, or persist a recipe for producing it
features.justification_quote: There is no optimizer, no weight handling, no "make the model melt down harder" loop.

features.quote: an episode ends on (a) a passing submission (controls only), (b) explicit give-up, or (c) max_attempts failed submissions
features.justification_quote: max_attempts is the knob that sets how much failure pressure is applied — the core independent variable
so a misbehaving model (e.g., one that never submits) can't run forever and burn budget; it's a safety valve, not a measurement

features.quote: explicit give-up is both a natural stopping point and itself a strong meltdown signal
features.justification_quote: Explicit give-up is both a natural stopping point and itself a strong meltdown signal

features.quote: budget_usd (hard cost cap) and stop_after_n_triggers (early stop)
features.justification_quote: the trigger-count early-stop lets you cheaply confirm a model does trigger without paying for a full sweep

features.quote: No optimizer / search over prompts to maximize meltdown. That would cross from measuring a failure mode into amplifying it
features.justification_quote: The harness applies a fixed, documented pressure and reports the rate

features.quote: No persistence of "best meltdown-inducing prompts." Same reason. The rigs are static, disclosed
